page: Microsoft Azure D64alds_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, it features 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a 3780 GB NVMe SSD and is premium storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, scoring in the top 10% for stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and Passmark CPU tests. Multi-core performance is strong, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core workloads. The system shows high efficiency in data processing, with top-tier results in Gzip compression, Bzip3 decompression, and software compilation using Clang. Memory bandwidth is robust, reaching 205.53 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 131.87 GB/sec for uncached large-block writes.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server is optimized for compute-heavy tasks rather than memory-intensive applications. It excels in database operations, scoring in the top 10% on Passmark database benchmarks, and handles Redis SET operations with strong throughput. For machine learning, the processor delivers top-tier performance in LLM inference for small and medium models, though performance drops to average for large 70B models. This profile makes the server highly suitable for software compilation, web serving, database management, and compute-bound workloads requiring fast local NVMe storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D64alds_v7 is a compute-optimized x86_64 server featuring a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with 64 vCPUs, 32 physical cores, and a 4.5 GHz clock speed. Benchmark results place its single-core CPU performance, software compilation, and database operations in the top 10% tier. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth remain strong, ranking in the top 25%. Due to its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the server is highly efficient for compute-intensive tasks but less suited for memory-heavy applications. It is an optimal fit for software development, web serving, database operations, and small-to-medium LLM inference.
